# Project Agent Rules

This file defines the baseline conventions that coding agents must follow in this repository.

## Scope

- These rules apply to every file in this repository unless a more specific rule overrides them.
- When a subproject has its own `AGENTS.md`, that file takes precedence for files under its directory.

## Language and Tone

- Respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in code, comments, or documentation.
- Keep responses clear and concise. Avoid unnecessary jargon.
- Use plain ASCII punctuation. Do not use the em dash character in code, comments, or user facing text.

## Code Style

- Follow the conventions already present in the file you are editing.
- Keep changes surgical. Do not reformat or rewrite unrelated code.
- Preserve existing comments. Do not delete or rewrite them during refactors.
- Extract repeated snippets into a shared helper when they appear in three or more places.
- Do not add compatibility re-exports when refactoring. Update all call sites instead.

## File Organization

- One concept belongs in one directory with one implementation. Do not create duplicate implementations.
- Keep files focused. Split files that grow beyond a reasonable size into smaller modules.
- Test files belong next to the code they test in this Go module.

## Testing and Verification

- Run the test suite after any code change.
- Add or update tests when behavior changes.
- Do not commit test artifacts into source directories.

## Git and Changes

- Respect recent user changes. Never revert or overwrite edits made by the user.
- Never access, deploy to, or assume a production environment. All work is local.
- Write commit messages in English, keeping conventional commit prefixes such as `feat:`, `fix:`, and `chore:` unchanged.

## Safety

- Never print or commit credentials, tokens, or other secrets.
- Do not question whether the user has already performed an action such as a commit or a deploy.
